subject.title: exec auto-reviewer re-bills a fresh model completion for every byte-identical repeated exec

question: May OpenClaw reuse model-backed exec reviewer decisions for byte-identical requests, and must that cache live only inside one reviewer/run with the full reviewed input as its key?
rationale: The redundant billing is source-backed, but caching an exec approval reviewer result changes approval-boundary semantics and needs explicit maintainer intent for cache lifetime, key shape, and scope.

options.title: Approve full-input per-run memo
options.body: Cache parsed reviewer decisions only inside the shared reviewer instance, keyed by the complete reviewed input or prompt, and never persist or convert them to durable approval.

options.title: Memoize allow-once only
options.body: Cache only low-risk allow-once results while leaving ask, error, and timeout decisions uncached for a narrower behavior change with fewer savings.

options.title: Keep fresh review semantics
options.body: Accept the repeated model cost to preserve one-request-one-review semantics until stronger security or live billing evidence is available.

recommendation.title: Approve full-input per-run memo
recommendation.body: Cache parsed reviewer decisions only inside the shared reviewer instance, keyed by the complete reviewed input or prompt, and never persist or convert them to durable approval.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame and recent exec approval history make vincentkoc the strongest available route for this approval-boundary decision.
